solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sad scene involving Net being withdrawn as punishment

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the reversed piece sits inside the shuffled letters
sad here means in a sorry state, so the letters of scene are knocked into a new order
withdrawn is read as drawn back, so the word Net is written backwards

explanation.surface: A gloomy scene at a fishing port, perhaps, where the net is being hauled back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad' looks like a mood but signals the anagram; 'being withdrawn' reverses Net, and 'involving' wraps the shuffled scene round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge passes a sentence, the penalty given to someone convicted of a crime.

clue.text: Contest well-matched over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: two sides that are well-matched are even

explanation.surface: A sports report calls a contest well-matched over its whole duration.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single competition at a sports meeting, such as the 100 metres.

clue.text: Tourist — one undressing? Not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the synonym for one undressing is left out, as the phrase says not at the start

parts.note: someone who undresses, especially as a performer, is a stripper

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a tourist is the one taking clothes off on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' removes the S from STRIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a British word for someone on a day trip or holiday outing, a sightseer.

clue.text: Upset Liberal in love

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, the political party; that the clue words also read backwards to give the letters is a coincidence of this parse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is upset at falling in love.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, love is the score of zero, meaning nothing at all.

clue.text: Spookery page one is circulating

indicators.note: circulating means moving round, so the letters of page one is go round into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front page about spying is going around.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooks are spies, so spookery is spying, the work of secret agents.

clue.text: On return secure this hotel accommodation

indicators.note: on return means coming back, so the synonym for secure is read backwards

parts.note: to secure a boat is to moor it

explanation.surface: A traveller, on coming back, books this hotel accommodation again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On return' turns MOOR backwards into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest stays in a room, a single unit of lodging at a hotel.

clue.text: Mountain chain called Eastern

parts.note: to have called someone on the phone is to have rang them

explanation.surface: A mountain chain is said to be called Eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line of connected mountains, like the Himalayas or the Andes.

clue.text: Formerly was victorious, we hear — it's brought up by the writer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the last piece is placed next to the rest
we hear says the next word is to be said aloud and spelt as its sound-alike

parts.note: someone who was victorious won

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the word it, with the 's standing for is, linking it to brought up
the writer of the clue refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: Someone who was once a winner says it was brought up by the author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals the sound-alike, 'brought up' reverses it, and 'the writer' is the setter speaking of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Onetime means former, describing what someone used to be, as in a onetime champion.

clue.text: Laid back about English knight's rejection of request

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the other letters
back means turned backwards, so the word Laid is reversed

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An easy-going knight, lying back, turns down a request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses Laid and 'about' puts it round the English knight; N for knight comes from chess notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal, saying no when someone asks for something.

clue.text: Think about artificial lake with some hesitation

parts.note: a pond is often a small man-made lake
er is the sound people make when they hesitate

explanation.surface: A council considers building an artificial lake, but hesitantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder is to consider or mull over something carefully.

clue.text: Discontinue stay

definitions.meaning: to discontinue something is to cease or end it
a stay or short visit, as in a ... for the night on a journey

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt a court's stay of proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to discontinue, and a brief pause somewhere on a journey is a halt of this kind.

clue.text: Upset the cop in referring to speech sounds

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the cop in are rearranged

explanation.surface: An upset police officer is being described, or perhaps a linguist upset the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic describes what relates to the sounds of human speech, as in the phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: Gift I'd carried for top politician

indicators.note: carried means held inside, so the gift contains the other piece

parts.note: a gift is a present
I'd written without its apostrophe gives the letters ID

explanation.surface: Someone carried a gift intended for a senior politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried' means the gift holds I'd inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of state in a republic such as the United States.

clue.text: Son coming into clean wealth

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something clean is pure
S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A son is about to come into a clean, untainted fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming into' means the son enters the word for clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Purse can mean money or funds available, as in the public purse.

clue.text: Drug substitute in location, outskirts of Bilbao

parts.note: a location is a place

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the first and last letters of the name are taken

explanation.surface: A substitute drug is being supplied somewhere on the edge of the Spanish city of Bilbao.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill given in place of a real medicine, often in trials.

clue.text: A lure, reportedly, to become less intense

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the phrase is spoken and spelt as its sound-alike

parts.note: a lure is a bait, so a lure is a bait

explanation.surface: A lure, so they say, makes something calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: When a storm or pain abates it dies down or lessens in strength.

clue.text: Alarm I'd set for navy man

indicators.note: set means arranged or put in order, so the letters of alarm I'd are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone set an alarm clock for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a senior officer commanding a fleet in a navy.

clue.text: Is participating in march — heaven!

indicators.note: participating in means taking part within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a march is a parade

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims what bliss it is to be taking part in a march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'participating in' puts Is inside the word for march.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the dwelling place of the blessed after death, a synonym for heaven.

clue.text: Some drear Gothic slang

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gloomy Gothic novel uses some slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the special jargon of a group, much like slang or cant.

clue.text: Friend's winning move

definitions.meaning: a friend is a pal or chum
in chess, checkmate, the move that wins the game

explanation.surface: A friend has made the decisive move in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is British slang for a pal, and in chess it is checkmate, ending the game.

clue.text: Oliver's decisive change of direction

definitions.meaning: Oliver ... is the orphan hero of the Dickens novel, so this is Oliver's surname
a sudden turn in a story or plot

explanation.surface: Oliver makes a firm change of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the Dickens orphan; a twist is an unexpected turn in events.

clue.text: Alliance at start letting each acceding Government use everything

indicators.note: at start means only the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.words: letting each acceding Government use everything

explanation.surface: A political alliance where each joining government gets full use of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a union of states or groups joined for a common purpose.

clue.text: Recluse in leather mittens

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A loner is wearing leather mittens.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone, cut off from society, often for religious reasons.

clue.text: One playing in poorish drama, humdrum ultimately

definitions.text: One playing in poorish drama, humdrum ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of each of the three words is taken

explanation.surface: An actor in a weak, dull play.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a ham overacts in second-rate shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a showy, overacting performer, the kind found in poor productions.

clue.text: Writer of verse protests in odd places

indicators.note: in odd places means taking the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word

explanation.surface: A versifier protests in some unlikely venues.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet composes poems, verses, as Keats or Wordsworth did.

clue.text: Worker from agency yet to arrive — a pattern

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker supplied by an agency
someone not yet arrived is late

explanation.surface: An agency temp who has not turned up yet is a familiar pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a model or guide shape used to make copies.
